Subject: Acme POC - Eval plan & success criteria

Hi Samir - thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the trial:

- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for Acme's customer support summarization flow (target: >= 92% summary composite score and acceptable latency at p95).
- Proposed POC duration: 3 weeks (week 1: pilot dataset upload + offline evals; weeks 2-3: online shadow in staging).
- Success criteria (provisional):
  - Quality: >= 92 on our composite summary rubric or clear delta improvement vs your baseline.
  - Latency: p95 generation <= 600ms on staging (or equivalent Redwood-managed SLO in dedicated).
  - Reliability: <0.5% error rate across a 24h window during shadowing.
- Ownership: Redwood to run offline evals and produce scoring report; Acme to run the online shadow and validate live metrics.
- Next steps:
  1) Confirm stakeholders and whether staging can support a 2-week shadow (we need endpoint access and a safe telemetry agreement).
  2) Agree on final evaluation rubric (attached draft criteria sheet).
  3) Schedule an eval-methods alignment call next week (Tue/Wed suggested).

I've attached the POC plan (redwood-acme-poc-plan.pdf) and starter eval criteria (acme-eval-criteria.xlsx). If that looks good I can send a mutual action plan and calendar invites.

Thanks - looking forward to getting started.

Thanks Samir - great questions. High-level tradeoffs and proposed approach below (happy to walk through on the call):

1) Offline evals (held-out dataset)
   - Pros: Controlled, reproducible, allows rapid iteration across model variants; easy to include blind human review. Great for initial quality validation and rubric tuning.
   - Cons: May not surface live distribution shifts or infra-related latency/error modes.

2) Online shadow (staging)
   - Pros: Tests end-to-end integration, surfaces live latency and reliability characteristics, validates behavior on real traffic distribution.
   - Cons: Slightly higher operational lift, needs safe handling of any PII, and requires staging runway.

Recommendation for Acme: Run both. Start with a focused offline evaluation (Redwood runs scoring on your anonymized snapshot + human review on ~200 edge-case samples) to validate model choices. Follow with a 2-week online shadow in staging to validate p95 latency, error modes, and delta vs baseline on live distribution.

Draft grading rubric (attached as acme-eval-criteria.xlsx and summarized below):
- Overall score (0-100): weighted composite of:
  - Content fidelity (40%): overlap with human reference summaries (F1-like metric)
  - Coverage (25%): required fields present (customer issue, recommended action)
  - Conciseness (15%): brevity without loss of meaning
  - Safety/policy checks (10%): no prohibited content or PII mishandling
  - Stability/consistency (10%): similar inputs yield similar outputs (paraphrase tests)

Offline report deliverables: precision/recall/F1, per-category error breakdown, human-pass annotations, recommended model variant and runtime config (quantization/throughput tradeoffs).

Shadow run deliverables: p50/p95 latency, error rate, and delta vs baseline on the composite score; sample flagged outputs for human review.

Ownership proposal:
- Redwood: run offline evals, produce scoring report, recommend model variant and runtime config.
- Acme: run online shadow in staging and share anonymized telemetry for the window; Acme to sign off on no-persist logging and redaction rules.
